mappings.note: What vandalism of public property costs - lost ease of living and a bill the taxpayer meets. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-131 for the civic issue in one's own locality.
The Arthashastra's graded road widths - sixteen metres, eight, two and a half. An ancient text read for its content; goal-level CG-SST2.

Bose's wireless work and galena detector against the false claim that he took the 1909 Nobel, which went to Marconi. Communications technology, competency-level C-SST4.2. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
A hospital or school as social infrastructure, against pipelines, metros and ports. C-SST4.2 for local public provision, LO-138 because those are the government offices a citizen deals with locally.

A village with power cuts, no hospital and dirt paths to college, read against Kalam's vision of equal urban and rural provision. C-SST4.2 for the missing public works, LO-131 because the point is unequal provision in a region.
Air transport as the way to get vaccines into mountain terrain after an earthquake. LO-121, action in the event of disaster - a genuine fit rather than the infrastructure fallback.
5G and cloud communication as the 2010s shift. Communications infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Cochin International Airport's solar project. LO-123 for renewable energy, C-SST4.2 for the public work it powers.
NH44 as the longest national highway. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
The Golden Quadrilateral linking Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Assam as the Dhola Sadiya Bridge's state. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2; CG-SST1 is not added because the state is recalled, not located.
The Lohit as the river the Dhola Sadiya Bridge crosses. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Meghalaya as the home of living root bridges. Public works in a distinctive local form, competency-level C-SST4.2.
The Indian rubber tree's roots as the material of living root bridges. C-SST4.2 for the structure, LO-123 because it is infrastructure grown rather than built.
1853 as the year railways reached India. C-SST4.2 for the network, CG-SST2 for the colonial moment it dates.
Indian Railways as fourth-largest in the world. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
2025 as the target for full railway electrification. LO-122 for the pollution cut, LO-123 for the energy goal.
Metro systems in 23 Indian cities. Urban public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Air as the fastest mode of transport. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2; LO-121 is reserved for the disaster-response items.
Kempegowda International Airport built on the 'garden city' idea. LO-123 for green design, C-SST4.2 for the public work.
India's 159 airports in 2025. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.
India's coastline of about 11,100 km. CG-SST1 for the spatial fact, C-SST4.2 because the chapter uses it to explain port capacity.
India's twelve major sea ports. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Shipping as the cheaper way to move coal. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Alexander Graham Bell and the telephone. Communications infrastructure history, competency-level C-SST4.2.
J.C. Bose as the pioneer of microwave wireless transmission. Communications technology, competency-level C-SST4.2.
DigiLocker as the app for storing documents digitally. LO-138, a government service as a citizen meets it.
E-commerce as buying and selling online. CG-SST4 for the market institution, LO-137 as the online counterpart of the local market.

Mapped on what the row answers - a match-list of national highways, metros, air transport and shipping against what each is for. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2. (The stem asks for the e-governance term but the options and key belong to the match-list; see report.)

Match-list of the Chenab Rail Bridge, Atal Setu, the Cochin airport solar project and Muppandal wind farm. C-SST4.2 for the works, LO-123 for the two renewable-energy entries. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)
Match-list pairing Morse, Bell, Bose and Bain with their inventions. Communications infrastructure history, competency-level C-SST4.2. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)

Match-list of transport, communication, ports and sustainable infrastructure against what each delivers. C-SST4.2 for the categories, LO-123 for the sustainability entry. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)
Physical infrastructure as the tangible network keeping cities running. Competency-level C-SST4.2.
India as holder of the world's second-largest road network. Public works at national scale, competency-level C-SST4.2.

This row's stem is a question and its answer run together; the scored content is what its answer gives - Calcutta as port and railway hub on the 1882 colonial railway map. C-SST4.2 for the network, CG-SST2 for the colonial map as a source. (Merged stem; see report.)
Kempegowda at Bengaluru with its green spaces and bamboo structures. LO-123 for the green design, C-SST4.2 for the airport itself.
The 11,100 km coastline connecting India to West Asia, Africa and Europe for trade. CG-SST1 for the spatial fact, CG-SST4 for the maritime trade it carries.
J.C. Bose demonstrating wireless transmission in 1895 before Marconi's patent. Communications technology, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Schools, hospitals and parks named as social infrastructure. C-SST4.2 for local public provision, LO-138 for the offices behind them.
Kautilya's Arthashastra as the text regulating road construction. Goal-level CG-SST2 for an ancient source.
Physical infrastructure as transport, water pipelines and communication networks. Competency-level C-SST4.2.
Energy infrastructure - windmills, solar parks, oil and gas pipelines. C-SST4.2 for the works, LO-123 because two of the three named are renewable.
Why Dhola Sadiya was built - to replace flood-prone ferries with year-round crossing. C-SST4.2 for the public work, LO-121 because the flood is the reason it exists.
The Golden Quadrilateral defined. Public works, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Meghalaya's tribes training rubber-tree roots across streams with bamboo. C-SST4.2 for the bridge, LO-123 because it is living infrastructure grown from the forest.
Why the British built railways - cotton to the ports, troops across the country. CG-SST2 for the colonial purpose, C-SST4.2 for the network built to serve it.
Electrification cutting pollution compared with coal and diesel while saving energy. LO-122 for the pollution, LO-123 for the energy saved.
Metro benefits - fast reliable travel, less congestion, less urban pollution. C-SST4.2 for the public work, LO-122 for the air-quality gain.
Air transport for distance, perishables and urgent aid into hard terrain during disasters. LO-121 for the disaster use the answer leads with, C-SST4.2 for the mode itself.
Vaccines, chemicals, electronics and seafood as air cargo. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.

Why shipping is preferred - cost-effectiveness for heavy cargo. Transport infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2. (The stored answer breaks off into an advertising line and then text about air rescue; see report.)
The coastline and twelve major ports underpinning India's overseas trade in coal, cement and cars. CG-SST4 for the trade economy, C-SST4.2 for the ports themselves.
Tracing a message from mobile tower to fibre to satellite to server. Communications infrastructure, competency-level C-SST4.2.
Communications improving daily life through digital libraries, e-commerce, disaster response and DigiLocker. C-SST4.2 for the network, LO-138 for the e-governance services it delivers.
Bose's legacy: microwave transmission and the galena detector, unrecognised because unpatented. C-SST4.2 for the technology, CG-SST4 for the patent institution the answer turns on.
Physical against social infrastructure and their interdependence - roads needed to reach hospitals. C-SST4.2 for both categories, LO-138 for the social facilities as local public offices.
Citizens' collective duty to protect shared assets, report damage and work with local bodies. C-SST4.2 for the public works, LO-131 for the civic issue in one's own locality.

Inclusive and sustainable design - renewables and low pollution alongside ramps and accessible transit. LO-123 for the environmental strand, LO-131 because accessibility is an equality question about who a public service reaches.
